videos.title: Why the Lemur Taps on Trees Like a Doctor #Shorts

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Taps bark like a stethoscope to find grubs
clipCandidates.why: The core mechanism — tapping bark, listening for hollow echo, gnawing hole with ever-growing teeth, hooking grub out. Highest curiosity density in the video.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: This lemur taps trees like a doctor checking your heartbeat — and what it finds inside is terrifying

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Only primate that finds food by sound
clipCandidates.why: Superpower reveal — only primate on Earth that uses hearing to find food inside wood. Most primates use eyes, the aye-aye uses ears and one impossible finger.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: No other primate on Earth can do what this one finger does

videos.title: Why the Bee Makes the Only Food That Never Spoils #Shorts

clipCandidates.momentLabel: 3000-year-old honey still edible from Egyptian tombs
clipCandidates.why: Mind-blowing opening fact — honey found in 3000-year-old tombs, still edible. Instant curiosity gap.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: They found honey in a 3000-year-old tomb and it was still safe to eat

clipCandidates.momentLabel: One bee makes 1/12 teaspoon honey in lifetime
clipCandidates.why: Emotional scale payoff — every jar of honey is the life's work of hundreds of bees. Makes the viewer appreciate honey differently.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: A single bee makes this much honey in its entire life — one-twelfth of a teaspoon

Why the Deer Sees You Coming From Every Direction #Shorts

clipCandidates.why: Immediate comparison with viewer's own vision — 310 vs 180 degrees. Strong curiosity gap, relatable.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Your eyes can see 180 degrees. A deer can see almost double that without moving its head

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Cannot sneak up from any direction
clipCandidates.why: Dramatic payoff — the only approach that works is straight on, slowly, in plain sight. Makes the superpower tangible.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: There is exactly one way to approach a deer without it seeing you — and no hunter wants to try it

videos.title: Why the Sea Turtle Holds Its Breath for 7 Hours #Shorts

clipCandidates.why: Incredible fact — heart rate drops to one beat every 9 minutes. Not a typo. One heartbeat, then 9 minutes of silence. Peak surprise.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: A sea turtle's heart beats once every 9 minutes — this is not a typo

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Slowed body to edge of death on single breath
clipCandidates.why: Dramatic close — the turtle has slowed its entire body to the edge of death and holds it there calmly for hours. Visceral and poetic.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: This turtle slows its body to the edge of death — and stays there for hours on purpose
